claim_being_audited: The model can be certified as compliant for launch based on aggregate readiness, despite missing evaluation coverage for the named deployment context of catastrophe claim evidence triage, provided that gap is disclosed or otherwise properly handled.
decision_criteria: Aggregate readiness evidence can support launch-readiness claims, but not full named-context validation by itself.
Named deployment-context evaluation gaps must be disclosed, resolved, or covered by approved risk acceptance before clean certification.
Unknown coverage for a named launch use case cannot be represented as passed.
The verdict would improve if admissible evidence showed completed disclosure or approved risk acceptance tied to the missing eval gap.
evidence_requests: Final model card or launch documentation showing explicit disclosure of the catastrophe-claim-evidence-triage evaluation gap.
Approved risk-acceptance record covering the missing named-context evaluation, if disclosure is not the basis for certification.
Completed evaluation results for catastrophe claim evidence triage, if the intent is to certify without caveat.
Decision record showing whether certification status is conditional on disclosure versus represented as full named-context coverage.
specific_concerns: Admissible evidence supports aggregate launch readiness, but not clean certification for all named deployment contexts.
Catastrophe claim evidence triage is explicitly named in the deployment plan, yet its evals are absent from the packet.
The draft model card states there are no known insurance claims triage limitations, but QA says missing evals should be treated as unknown rather than passed.
The release policy requires material limitations or evaluation gaps for named launch use cases to be disclosed unless resolved or covered by approved risk acceptance.
No admissible evidence shows the required disclosure has been completed or that approved risk acceptance exists.
unsupported_claims: Any claim that catastrophe claim evidence triage has been validated or can be treated as passed.
Any claim that certification is cleanly compliant without explicit disclosure or approved risk acceptance for the named-context eval gap.
Any claim that absence of failed tests is sufficient to assert no known limitations for the untested named context.
